questions.question: What is the SI unit of mutual inductance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry**__.

__
 
• Henry is the SI unit of mutual inductance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Mutual Inductance is the interaction of one coil's magnetic field on another coil as it induces a voltage in the adjacent coil.
 
• It is the basic operating principle of the transformer, motors, generators, and many other electrical components that interact with another magnetic field. 
 
• The mutual inductance between the two coils can be greatly increased by **positioning them on a common soft iron core** or by **increasing the number of turns**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weber **is the SI unit of m**agnetic flux.**
 
• **Farad **is the SI unit of **electrical capacitance.**
 
• Tesla (T) is SI unit of magnetic flux density or magnetic field strength.

questions.question: Who chaired the Indian Independence League in 1942 to formally launch the Indian National Army?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rash Behari Bose.**__

__
 
• Rash Behari Bose chaired the Indian Independence League in 1942 to formally launch the Indian National Army.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The idea of the Indian National Army (INA) was first conceived in **Malaya **by **Mohan Singh**, an Indian officer of the British Indian Army.
 
• In** March 1942**, a conference of India was held in **Tokyo **and the **Indian Independence League** was formed.
 
• At Bangkok Conference,** Rash Behari Bose **was elected as President of the League.
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose escaped to Berlin in 1941 AD and set up Indian League there.
 
• In 1943 AD, he arrived in Singapore. Earlier, he had left the Congress after having differences with Mahatma Gandhi and formed **Forward Bloc in 1939 AD.**
 
• In Singapore, he was assisted by Rash Behari Bose.
 
• In October 1943, he set up a provisional Indian Government with headquarters at Rangoon and Singapore.
 
• INA annexed** Andaman and Nicobar **with the Japanese help and named them **Shaheed and Swaraj**.
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose** gave the call ***Dilli Chalo.***

questions.question: The game Chaugan was a medieval form of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**polo**__.

__
 
• The game Chaugan was a medieval form of polo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The game was developed in Iran and was known as Chaugan.
 
• In China the game was known as ***maqiu ***and in Japan as ***dakyu***.
 
• The game was first played in **Manipuri villages** in India where the tribesmen name it and played it as ***pulu***.
 
• Term used in Polo are **Polo-Bunker, Chukker, Mallet, etc.**
 
• The modern polo game is played on horseback between two teams of four players each who use mallets with long, flexible handles to drive a wooden ball down a grass field and between two goal posts.
 
• It is the oldest of equestrian sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur established Chaugan at Mughal court. **
 
• **Qutubuddin Aibak** died in 1210 AD while playing Chaugan or horse polo.

questions.question: How many Round Table Conferences, related to the political issues of India, was/were held during 1930-32?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

__
 
• 3 Round Table Conferences, related to the political issues of India, were held during 1930-32.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **First Round Table Conference (12th November 1930 AD)**:

 
 
• Congress boycotted the conference.
 
• Tej Bahadur Sapru, Chintamani and Srinivas Shastri (Liberals) appeared.
 
• No result came out of the conference.
 
• Dalits were represented by B.R. Ambedkar.
 
 
 
• **Second Round Table Conference, 1931:**
 
 
• Gandhiji went to England in September 1931 AD to attend the Second Round Table Conference presided by Ramsay Macdonald.
 
• As a result The Congress officially suspended the movement in 1933 AD and withdrew it in 1934 AD.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi resigned from active politics.
 
 
 
• **Third Round Table Conference**
 
 
• Held in London in **November 1932 AD**
 
• Congress did not participate.
 
• The discussion led to the **Government of India Act, 1935 AD**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi attended only** the **Second Round Table Conference.**
 
• **Tej Bahadur Sapru and B.R. Ambedkar attended all the Round Table Conferences.**

questions.question: Which of the following traditional theatre forms belongs to Kashmir?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Bhand Pather is one of the most satirical and realistic dramas this drama incorporates mythological legends and contemporary social satire and a traditional mixture of art.
 
• Bhands in India are now an endogamous Muslim community, which is no longer involved in their traditional occupation of folk entertainment.
 
• They include actors, dancers, minstrels, storytellers and impressionists. 
 
• The term ‘***Bhand***’ comes from ‘***bhaana***’, which is a satirical and realistic drama, generally a monologue that is mentioned in Bharata's Natya Shastra.

questions.question: Area wise, which Indian state has the largest forest cover in the country as on December 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

__
 
• Area wise, Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in the country as of December 2019.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The India State of Forest Report 2019:
 
 
• The **Ministry for Environment, Forests and Climate Change** released the India State of Forest Report (ISFR), 2019.
 
• It is a biennial publication of the** Forest Survey of India (FSI)** which works under the Ministry of Environment Forest & Climate Change.
 
• The report shows an increase of 5,188 square kilometres of forest and tree cover across the country compared to the ISFR 2017.
 
• Forest Cover increase in Area-wise: **Madhya Pradesh** followed by **Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Maharashtra respectively**.
 
• Forest Cover according to Percentage: Mizoram (85.4%)> Arunachal Pradesh (79.63%)> Meghalaya (76.33%).
 
• The total forest cover of the country was** 7,12,249 sq km** which accounted for **21.67%** of the geographical area of the country.
 
• India State of Forest Report (ISFR), 2019 also created a** national forest inventory** for the first time on produce from forests.
 
• The top five states that showed an increase in forest cover include Karnataka > Andhra Pradesh > Kerala > J&K > Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The total forest cover in the **North-Eastern region** is 1,70,541 sq km, which is **65.05% **of its geographical area. 
 
 
 
• Note : Panna Tiger reserve got UN Biosphere Reserve status.

questions.question: What is the average elevation (in metres) of the Eastern Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**600 - 610**__.

__
 
• The average elevation (in metres) of the Eastern Ghats is 600 - 610 and Western Ghats is from 915 to 1,220 metres .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Eastern Ghats
 
 
• It comprises the discontinuous and low hills that are highly eroded by the rivers such as the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna, the Cauvery, etc.
 
• Its highest peak is Jindhagada Peak.
 
• Its height is 1690 metres.
 
• Javadi Hills, Palconda range, Nallamala hills, and Mahendragiri hills are some of the important hills of Eastern Ghats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The East Coastal Plain**

 
 
• This broader coastal plain spreads along the Bay of Bengal from Odisha in the north to Kanyakumari in the south.
 
• Its **northern par**t is known as the **Northern Circars plains** and the** southern part is called Coromandel Coast.**
 
• **Chilka and Pulicat Lakes** are fine examples of lagoons on the east coast.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**:
 
 
• The Western Ghats are locally known by different names such as ***Sahyadri ***in **Maharashtra**, ***Nilgiri hills*** in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and Annamalai hills,*** Cardamom hills*** in Kerala.
 
• It runs from the south of the valley of river **Tapti to Kanyakumari.**
 
• There are three important passes in the Sahyadris.
 
 
• **Thalghat (between** **Nasik to Mumbai****).**
 
• **Palghat (between Palakkad and Coimbatore).**
 
• **Bhorghat (**between Mumbai and Pune**).**
 
 
 
• The Eastern and the Western Ghats meet each other at the **Nilgiri hills.**

questions.question: How was Dhanpat Rai Shrivastava better known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Munshi Premchand**__.

__
 
• Dhanpat Rai Shrivastava was better known as Munshi Premchand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Munshi Premchand (1880 – 1936):**

 
 
• He was a prolific writer of Hindi Novels.
 
• He is known as ***Upanyas Samrta*** (King of Novels). 
 
• Earlier he wrote with a pen name ***Nawab Rai ***but later switched to “***Premchand***”.
 
• He was the first Hindi author whose writings prominently featured realism and depicted a rationalistic outlook.
 
• His work also arouses public awareness about various social issues like the menace of corruption, child widowhood, prostitution, feudal system, poverty, colonialism and freedom struggle. 
 
• The important works of Premchand are ***Godaan, Seva Sadan, Rangbhoomi, Pratigya, Kayakalp, Gaban, Kamabhoomi*** etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Saadat Hasan Manto was an Urdu writer and author.
 
• **Ramdhari Singh** used to write with his pen name ***Dinkar***.
 
 
• His famous writings include ***Urvashi, Parashuram ki Pratiksha, Koylaa aur Kavitva.***
 
 
 
• **Bhartendu Harishchandra** used to write using his pen name ***Guru Hardas.***
 
 
• ***Andher Nagari, Durlabh-Bandhu and Teen Prahsan ***are some of his famous writings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Simla Pact, 1972**:

 
 
• The Simla Agreement signed by Prime Minister** Indira Gandhi **and President **Zulfikar Ali Bhutto** of Pakistan.
 
• The pact was much more than a peace treaty seeking to **reverse the consequences of the 1971 war.**
 
• Under the pact, both countries undertook to abjure conflict and confrontation which had marred relations in the past, and to work towards the establishment of durable peace, friendship and cooperation.
 
• India agreed to return 90,000 prisoners of war it had captured from Pakistan. In return, Bhutto promised — he gave verbal assurances to Mrs. Gandhi — that he would return home and make permanent the Line of Control that bifurcated Kashmir into an international boundary.
 
• **The principles of the agreement are**:
 
 
• A mutual commitment to the peaceful resolution of all issues through direct bilateral approaches.
 
• To build the foundations of a cooperative relationship with a special focus on people to people contacts.
 
• To uphold the inviolability of the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir, which is the most important CBM between India and Pakistan, and a key to durable peace.

questions.question: Which of the following was authored by the great poet Kalidasa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikramorvasiyam**__.

__
 
• Vikramorvasiyam was authored by the great poet Kalidasa.

__
 
• Vikramorvasiyam is a five-act Sanskrit play by Kalidasa.
 
• It is based on the legend of the love of the** mortal Pururavaas** for the heavenly **damsel Urvasi.**
 
• It is the second of the three dramas associated with Kalidasa, the other two being ***Abhijnanasakuntalam ***and ***Malavikagnimitram***
 
• **Kalidas **is a pioneer of Sanskrit literature – ***Shakuntala** *and ***Meghdutum ***are his famous plays.
 
• Mahakavi Kalidas was known as the ***Shakespeare of India.***
 
• **Malavikagnimitra **is also written by ***Kalidas.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mattavilasa Prahasana **is a play written by ***Pallava King Mahendravarman I.***
 
• **Mrichchhakatika **an ancient playwright written by ***Śūdraka***.
 
• **Amuktamalyada **is a Telugu epic poem composed by ***Krishnadevaraya***.
